explain.say: Imagine standing on a high diving board. Your heart pounds and you want to climb down! That big, wobbly feeling is anxiety, which means worry that feels very strong in your body. Look at the line on the board. It shows how anxious you feel over time.

faq.q: What is the difference between worry and anxiety?
faq.a: Worry is the thinking part: the what-if thoughts. Anxiety is when that worry becomes a strong feeling in your body too, like a racing heart, a tight chest or a sick tummy.
asks: Is anxiety the same as worry?

faq.q: How long does a wave of anxiety last?
faq.a: The strongest part often passes in a few minutes, and most waves settle within about half an hour. Remembering that it will pass can make it less scary.
asks: Will this anxious feeling go away?

faq.q: How can I help a wave of anxiety pass?
faq.a: Breathe slowly, feel your feet on the floor, and name five things you can see. Remind yourself: this feeling is uncomfortable, but it will pass.
asks: What helps when I feel anxious?

faq.q: When should I get help for anxiety?
faq.a: If anxiety lasts for weeks, feels too big, or stops you going to school, sleeping or seeing friends, talk to a trusted grown-up, a school counsellor or a doctor. They can help.
asks: Do I need help for my anxiety?

faq.a: No. Anxiety is not your fault and it does not mean you are weak. It is your brain's alarm being extra careful, and it can be helped.
asks: Am I weak if I feel anxious?

facts: The World Health Organization estimated that about 300 million people worldwide lived with an anxiety disorder in 2019, making it one of the most common health conditions.
Psychologists have found that facing a feared situation step by step usually makes the anxiety smaller each time.
